mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate borrowing and investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If 20-day forward returns are not higher than baseline during periods of low FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a strong labor market, which may boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE drops below 4% but 20-day returns are not positive in >60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is high and the unemployment rate is low, it may indicate controlled inflation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the joint condition of high FEDFUNDS and low UNRATE does not correlate with positive 60-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GDP during a late-cycle expansion may indicate sustained economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth does not predict positive 60-day returns during late-cycle periods.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment suggests economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases but 5-day returns are not positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production above 100 indicates strong supply activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO exceeds 100 but 20-day returns are not positive in >60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When real estate sentiment increases and federal funds rate is low, it may boost consumption, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS and FEDFUNDS do not jointly predict positive 60-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate during early recovery may indicate underutilized labor, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE exceeds 5% but 20-day returns are not negative in >60% of cases.
